title: SharePoint: Agent Chat web part embeds Microsoft 365 Copilot agents in pages
summary: The briefing's rollout, licensing and agent-blocking controls are supported. Two wording clarifications would distinguish the notice's no-action requirement from an undocumented switch and make the documented limits of the web-part disabling parameter explicit.

claims.claim: Agent Chat is a new web part for modern SharePoint page editors.
claims.quote: This is a new web part available for modern page editors in SharePoint.

claims.claim: The roadmap says the web part can be configured to use any Microsoft 365 Copilot agent.
claims.quote: The web part can be configured to use any M365 Copilot agent.

claims.claim: Microsoft published notice MC1559633 on 18 November 2026.
claims.quote: Published 2026-11-18; last updated 2026-11-18

claims.claim: SharePoint Online page authors add the web part through the standard page editing experience.
claims.quote: Platforms/Services: SharePoint Online, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Microsoft Copilot Studio. What will happen: SharePoint page authors can add the Agent Chat web part to pages using the standard page editing experience.

claims.claim: Authors select published agents already available to them in Microsoft 365 Copilot.
claims.quote: Authors can select published agents already available to them in Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.claim: The web part embeds existing Microsoft 365 Copilot agents so users can chat directly on SharePoint pages.
claims.quote: We're introducing the Agent Chat web part in SharePoint, allowing organizations to embed their existing Microsoft 365 Copilot agents directly into SharePoint pages.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Users can continue their conversations in a full-screen chat experience.
claims.quote: Users can interact with agents directly from SharePoint pages and continue conversations in a full-screen chat experience.

claims.quote: Existing SharePoint page permissions and agent access permissions remain independent.

claims.quote: Adding an agent to a page does not automatically grant users access to that agent.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: SharePoint page content is not automatically passed to the agent.
claims.quote: SharePoint page content is not automatically passed to the agent.

claims.quote: SharePoint does not store Copilot agent chat data or change how agent data is processed.

claims.claim: The change does not change how agent data is processed.
claims.quote: SharePoint does not store Copilot agent chat data or change how agent data is processed.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: No admin action is required before rollout, and the web part becomes available as part of rollout.
claims.quote: No admin action is required before rollout. The Agent Chat web part becomes available as part of the rollout.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends informing SharePoint page authors and support teams.
claims.quote: We recommend informing SharePoint page authors and support teams about this capability

claims.claim: The notice sets no act-by date.
claims.quote: Act by: none

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: The default is user-opt-in: page authors choose to add the available web part before it affects their pages.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Agent Chat" "SharePoint" disable block admin tenant site'. Read MC1559633, Manage access to agents in SharePoint and Set-SPOTenant; no web-part activation switch found. The notice says authors can add it.

claims.claim: The feature's licensing model is per-user.
claims.quote: Who is affected: SharePoint page authors who want to embed Copilot agents. Users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license and access to the configured agent.

claims.where: summary; licensing.notes; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Scope; rationale: cost and impact
claims.claim: The notice identifies users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence and access to the configured agent as the affected users.
claims.quote: Who is affected: SharePoint page authors who want to embed Copilot agents. Users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license and access to the configured agent.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Meter; rationale: cost; Open questions
claims.claim: No price, credit rate or meter specific to the Agent Chat web part was found published at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: 'SharePoint "Agent Chat web part" "billing"'. Read Licensing for agents powered by the standard harness and MC1559633; results describe agent billing generally, not a web-part-specific rate.

claims.claim: No Microsoft Learn page describing the Agent Chat web part was found in searches.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Agent Chat web part"'. Results concerned other chat products or agents generally; opened Manage access to agents in SharePoint and Set-SPOTenant, neither of which describes this web part.

claims.claim: An agent's configured capabilities define the scope of its accessible knowledge sources.
claims.quote: The Agent Capabilities section displays the configured capabilities for the agent, defining the scope of its accessible knowledge sources.

claims.claim: Agents can have configured actions that can be reviewed.
claims.quote: Agent actions display the action ID and version number, configured functions for the action, along with their matching and selection status.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: The web part's calling identity and sign-in behaviour are not documented in the material found.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Agent Chat web part" authentication user identity approval'. Read MC1559633 and Manage access to agents in SharePoint; neither describes this web part's calling identity or sign-in flow.

claims.claim: The notice does not describe any approval step added by the web part.
claims.quote: Authors can select published agents already available to them in Microsoft 365 Copilot. Users can interact with agents directly from SharePoint pages and continue conversations in a full-screen chat experience.

claims.claim: The notice states no admin switch for the web part.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Agent Chat" "SharePoint" disable block admin tenant site'. Read MC1559633, Manage access to agents in SharePoint and Set-SPOTenant. No web-part-specific switch found; the notice says no admin action is required.
claims.fix: Replace 'the notice states no admin switch for it' with 'the notice says no admin action is required before rollout'. This avoids presenting the notice's silence as an explicit statement that a switch does not exist.

claims.claim: The Block control is in Microsoft 365 admin center under Agents > All agents > agent > Block.
claims.quote: Select Agents > All agents. In the All agents page, select an agent from the list of agents. In the agent details pane that opens, immediately under the agent's name, select Block or Unblock.

claims.claim: POST /beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks a Copilot package to prevent its usage.
claims.quote: Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage. POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: Blocking is an existing organization-wide control for the selected agent.
claims.quote: Block or unblock agents for the entire organization by using the same controls that work for any other app in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: For agents created in SharePoint or Foundry, blocking affects availability in Microsoft Copilot Chat only.
claims.quote: However, blocking an agent that you created by using SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry only impacts its availability in Microsoft Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: The block API supports Global service but not US Government L4, US Government L5 (DOD) or China operated by 21Vianet.
claims.quote:
| Global service | US Government L4 | US Government L5 (DOD) | China operated by 21Vianet | 
| ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |

claims.claim: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

claims.claim: The block operation uses the preview beta API.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: The documentation does not explicitly state whether blocking removes an agent from the Agent Chat web part.
claims.quote: Searched: 'SharePoint "Agent Chat web part" "Block"'. Read agent-actions and Manage access to agents in SharePoint: they distinguish blocking by agent origin and limit SharePoint-created agents to Copilot Chat, but neither explicitly describes removal from the new web part.

claims.claim: The Set-SPOTenant reference lists a -DisabledWebPartIds parameter.
claims.quote:
### -DisabledWebPartIds
Allows administrators to prevent certain web parts from being added to pages or rendering on pages on which they were previously added.

claims.claim: No page found says -DisabledWebPartIds covers Agent Chat or gives its web part ID.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Set-SPOTenant DisabledWebPartIds Agent Chat web part'. Read -DisabledWebPartIds and searched the reference for Agent Chat: the supported list contains Amazon Kindle, YouTube, Twitter, Embed, Microsoft Bookings and Stream, not Agent Chat.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence beginning 'The Set-SPOTenant reference lists' with 'The Set-SPOTenant reference documents -DisabledWebPartIds for Amazon Kindle, YouTube, Twitter, Embed, Microsoft Bookings and Stream only; it does not list Agent Chat.' The reference explicitly limits the supported web parts, rather than merely omitting an ID.

claims.claim: No Microsoft Learn setting named specifically for this web part was found.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Agent Chat" "SharePoint" disable block admin tenant site'. Read Manage access to agents in SharePoint, agent-actions and Set-SPOTenant; found general agent controls but no setting named for this web part.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio documents billing conditions for agents used in SharePoint.
claims.quote: If you have a Microsoft 365 Copilot license, using agents in Copilot Chat, Microsoft Teams, or SharePoint for classic answers, generative answers, or Microsoft Graph tenant grounding isn't charged when the agent runs with your authenticated identity.
